data.title: World Brief · Friday, November 13, 2026
data.subtitle: Prepared 19:05 ET

items.title: Expectations of a Fed rate hike are strengthening
items.text: October PPI came in slightly below expectations at 0.3% month over month, but at 6.5% year over year it is the highest since 2022. After the hot CPI, markets are pricing a hike at the December 9 meeting; the 10-year yield settling above 5% directly pushes up mortgage and credit costs.

items.title: Jensen Huang resigns at Nvidia
items.text: The founder and CEO stepped down on Thursday after allegations about workplace relationships and a link to a person suspected of spying for China; CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO. Support is growing in Congress for tighter chip export restrictions, and the company's market value fell below $4 trillion.

items.title: US-Iran tension is escalating
items.text: The Revolutionary Guards said they struck a US early-warning radar in Bahrain; the US denied it. Trump said there is no need for a deal with Iran; supply and shipping risk in the region is the main reason Brent is holding around $96.

items.title: Russia-Ukraine: diplomacy and strikes side by side
items.text: While US envoys met with Putin and Zelensky, the two sides traded strikes through the night. Even so, agreement was reached on a prisoner swap that Zelensky called the largest of the war.

items.title: Politics in Washington
items.text: An attempt in the House to impeach Defense Secretary Hegseth failed for lack of Republican support. In the midterms, Mississippi elected a Democratic senator (Scott Colom) for the first time since 1982.

data.title: World Brief · Thursday, November 12, 2026
data.subtitle: Prepared 19:00 ET

items.title: Jensen Huang resigns from Nvidia
items.text: Huang, under a board investigation over his relationship with an executive suspected of working for China, left as CEO and board member effective immediately. The stock fell 14% at the open and closed down 4.34%; Semafor reported the Justice Department is separately running an antitrust review. The leadership vacuum at the stock carrying the AI rally adds uncertainty before earnings on November 17.

items.title: Bond sell-off: 10-year above 5%, December hike nearly priced in
items.text: Tuesday's October CPI beat expectations at 0.4% month over month (core 0.3%); per CME FedWatch, the odds of a 25 bp hike in December are ~90% and of 50 bp ~9%. Waller putting 50 bp on the table pushed the short end sharply higher (2-year +15 bp). Direct pressure on mortgage and credit costs.

items.title: Trump: "We don't need a deal with Iran"
items.text: As US overnight strikes on Iran entered their 12th day, the Houthis said they hit two Saudi tankers in the Red Sea; Trump threatened Iran and the Houthis with heavy military punishment if it happens again. Bab el-Mandeb carries ~12% of world trade, a new risk front for oil and inflation expectations.

items.title: Dollar at a 19-month high, euro weak
items.text: The dollar index rose above 103, its highest since April 2025; the euro fell below 1.11 and USD/JPY approached 160. The Fed-ECB rate gap is expected to widen, and Japan keeps up its warnings on the yen.

items.title: Europe at a record, Anthropic IPO nears
items.text: The Stoxx 600, light on tech, closed at a record 664.01 despite the Nvidia shock. Renaissance Capital expects the Anthropic IPO to price in the week of November 16; however, Reuters reported the company withdrew the $70-80 range it had given banks and that new pricing will be announced soon.

data.title: World Brief · Wednesday, November 11, 2026
data.subtitle: Prepared 19:05 ET

items.title: A Fed hike is on the table
items.text: October CPI came in at 0.35% month over month and core at 0.30%; the 10-year yield rose ~12 bp on Tuesday back to 5% and the 2-year jumped ~20 bp. Markets almost fully price a hike at the December meeting, and a Fed official said inflation is broadening. A critical week for rate volatility.

items.title: Leadership crisis at Nvidia
items.text: According to the WSJ, the board is preparing to oust Jensen Huang; Huang admitted infidelity in a note to employees on Sunday, and the board is investigating with outside counsel whether he was a foreign-intelligence target. The stock closed up 2.9% and fell ~8% after hours; Baird cut it to Neutral. Given its index weight, this directly affects the S&P and the Nasdaq.

items.title: Anthropic IPO approaches
items.text: The company set a price range of $70-78; the top end implies a valuation of ~$1.4 trillion. Reports say trading could begin around November 19 and the range could be raised if demand is strong. One of the largest IPOs in history and a litmus test for AI valuations.

items.title: Washington after the midterms
items.text: Democrats took control of the House and the Senate (Senate 54-44, with Mississippi and Alaska still counting). Republicans elected Jim Jordan minority leader from January; the impeachment resolution against Defense Secretary Hegseth was sent back to committee by 211-204. Divided government will complicate budget and fiscal fights.

items.title: Iran and Ukraine fronts
items.text: Iran-linked tanker attacks and Hormuz disruptions are supporting oil; France blamed the Revolutionary Guards for cyberattacks on supermarket refrigerators. US-Ukraine-Russia talks in Abu Dhabi ended with agreement on a large prisoner swap; stray drones over the Baltic scrambled NATO jets.

data.title: World Brief · Tuesday, November 10, 2026
data.subtitle: Prepared 19:02 ET

items.title: Odds of a Fed hike are firming
items.text: After hotter-than-expected core inflation (October CPI +0.4% month over month vs 0.3% expected; core +0.3% vs 0.2%), Governor Waller said he leans toward at least a 25 basis point hike in December and that 50 should be considered; Dallas Fed's Logan argued two more hikes are needed. The Fed meets December 8-9, and short-term yields (2-year +17 bp) are pricing it in.

items.title: Trump: Iran war is "effectively over"; Tehran denies talks
items.text: Trump said new strikes are unlikely but the naval blockade will continue; Iran said no meeting is planned in Qatar. Brent fell below $92, which matters for energy prices and the inflation outlook.

items.title: Russia and Ukraine at the table in Abu Dhabi
items.text: In the first US-mediated meeting since February, Kushner said the sides narrowed the gap between them; the White House is "cautiously optimistic". A headline to watch for European risk and energy.

items.title: Nvidia board investigation
items.text: The board opened an independent investigation into allegations that CEO Jensen Huang was a target of foreign intelligence; Huang acknowledged a mistake in his private life in an email to employees. The stock fell 5.5% and its market value dipped below $4 trillion intraday.

items.title: US politics: post-election tension
items.text: After the midterms in which Democrats won Congress, Trump posted messages questioning the integrity of the results; Republican Rep. Massie filed eight articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Hegseth.

data.title: World Brief · Monday, November 9, 2026
data.subtitle: Prepared 19:05 ET

items.title: Trump: Iran war is militarily "effectively over"
items.text: After meeting Qatar's prime minister, Trump said a new strike is very unlikely while talks continue; Brent fell 5.5% to below $93. But attacks on ships around Hormuz continue and the Houthis claimed an attack on Aramco offices in Riyadh, so the drop in oil is fragile.

items.title: Nvidia board opens probe into Jensen Huang
items.text: The board launched an independent review over allegations about Huang's relationship with a businessperson suspected of gathering information for China; Trump said the FBI is looking into it but that Huang "will be fine". The stock fell 4.6% (~$200 billion in value). The company said it sees no sign of leaked secrets and China rejected the claims; the allegations are not proven.

items.title: Washington wakes up to a new balance
items.text: Congress convened this week after Democrats won both chambers in the midterms; Trump made Stephen Miller White House chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles. Republican Thomas Massie filed impeachment articles against Defense Secretary Hegseth over the Iran war, and a House vote may be forced.

items.title: Fed: a December hike is being priced in
items.text: The Fed raised rates 25 basis points in September and held at 3.75-4.00% in October; futures put the odds of another hike in December at ~80%. Tuesday's October CPI at 08:30 ET is critical; because of the 2025 shutdown, no annual rate will be published this time.

items.title: Race to succeed Lagarde at the ECB
items.text: Euro area finance ministers (Eurogroup) reviewed candidates for when Lagarde leaves on February 7, 2027; Klaas Knot and BIS chief Pablo Hernandez de Cos are the front-runners. The choice matters for the euro and Europe's rate path; the euro approached 1.12.

data.title: World Brief · Sunday, November 8, 2026
data.subtitle: Prepared 19:02 ET

items.title: US extends Iran blockade to land routes
items.text: CENTCOM set up the "Iron Gate" task force to track Iran's overland transfers of weapons and sanctioned goods; on Saturday a cargo ship trying to run the blockade in the Gulf of Oman was disabled. Trump said "small-scale" strikes hit Qeshm island but there will be no return to full war, while Rubio said a deal may not be possible. This risk is the main reason Brent is holding near $98.

items.title: Strong jobs data lifts Fed rate-hike expectations
items.text: Nonfarm payrolls rose 165,000 in October (expected ~60,000) and unemployment fell to 4.1%. Markets put ~80% odds on a 25 basis point hike at the December 9 FOMC; Tuesday's CPI (expected 0.3% month over month) can confirm or upset that pricing.

items.title: Congress goes to the Democrats; AI stocks under pressure
items.text: Democrats took control of the House and the Senate in the midterms, so Trump's last two years will be spent under divided government. Expectations of AI regulation, driven by worries over data centers and electricity bills, were one of the triggers of Thursday's chip sell-off.

items.title: Russia-Ukraine: talks in Abu Dhabi, strikes on Kyiv
items.text: US, Russian and Ukrainian delegations will meet in Abu Dhabi on November 10-11; the EU rejected the security deal with Russia proposed by Trump. Zelensky said North Korean missiles were used in overnight strikes on the Kyiv region.

items.title: Israel: Eisenkot to be asked to form a government
items.text: President Herzog will task Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming a government after the election; the transition to a post-Netanyahu era could reshape regional diplomacy. Separately, 6 people were killed in a shooting in Krakow, Poland.

data.title: World Brief · Saturday, November 7, 2026
data.subtitle: Prepared 19:05 ET

items.title: Democrats take both chambers of Congress
items.text: Democrats won both the House and the Senate in the midterms; the new Congress takes office in January. Vice President Vance largely blamed the defeat on the Iran war, while Trump signaled he is ready to fight the new majority. The risk of gridlock in 2027 over the budget, the debt ceiling and investigations is rising.

items.title: US strikes Iran's Qeshm island again
items.text: Two missiles hit Qeshm, at the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz, on Friday night; Trump called it a "small" operation targeting an air-defense asset. According to UKMTO, 11 ships were attacked in the area last week and 3 sank; transits are ~65% below pre-war levels. Qatari mediation continues, and Iran has set 7 conditions for reopening the strait. This is the main risk for oil pricing.

items.title: Jobs surprise: +165,000 in October
items.text: Nonfarm payrolls rose 165,000 against expectations of ~59,000-65,000, and unemployment fell from 4.2% to 4.1%. The strong data reinforced expectations that the Fed will not rush to cut rates; yields and the dollar rose. Michigan consumer sentiment rose to 51, and 1-year inflation expectations eased to 4.3%.

items.title: AI/chip sell-off: Nasdaq's worst week since June
items.text: The Nasdaq fell ~5.5% and the chip index ~12% on Thursday; despite Friday's rebound (AMD +11%), the Nasdaq ended the week down 3.4%. Concerns that new restrictions on data-center construction could follow the Democratic win weighed on AI investment expectations; the VIX is around 25.6.

items.title: Shooting in Krakow, Poland
items.text: On Saturday afternoon an attacker drove into the Main Market Square and opened fire at random: at least 6 people were killed and 15 wounded. The suspect, a Polish citizen, was shot and detained by police; no motive has been announced yet.

items.title: US jobs crush expectations
items.text: Nonfarm payrolls rose 165,000 in October (consensus ~59,000) and unemployment came in at 4.1%. Markets now price a higher chance of a Fed rate hike in December, which feeds directly into short-term rates and currency risk.

items.title: Partial rebound after the AI sell-off
items.text: After the Nasdaq fell more than 5.5% on Thursday and entered correction territory, it recovered 1.1% today, led by chipmakers. In Asia, the Kospi and Nikkei plunged about 6%. The sell-off was triggered by fears of tighter regulation after AI-critical candidates won in the midterms.

items.title: Midterms: Congress flips to the Democrats
items.text: According to CBS and NBC, Democrats won majorities in both the House and the Senate; some races are still being counted. Jeffries expects at least 255 seats. Trump's 2027 agenda (taxes, budget, regulation) now has to pass a divided Congress.

items.title: Iran war: threats and diplomacy side by side
items.text: Trump said the US may have to destroy the rest of Iran; meanwhile, Iran has reportedly sent a nuclear proposal via Qatar that Washington is reviewing. Two tankers hit mines and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz; Brent is holding near $98.

items.title: Corporate front
items.text: Oracle fell on reports that Microsoft ended a computing contract; Tesla will end Cybertruck production in Texas by mid-next year to make room for the Cybercab. Moderna beat third-quarter expectations and raised its 2026 revenue target.
